literal: Good when becoming as good things those who see, bad when becoming sorrow experiencing why?
translation: Those who gladly accept good fortune as a natural occurrence, why should they suffer sorrow when bad fortune strikes?
modern: நன்மைகள் நடக்கும்போது அவற்றை இயல்பான நல்லவையாக ஏற்றுக்கொள்பவர்கள், தீமைகள் நடக்கும்போது மட்டும் துன்பப்பட்டு கலங்குவது ஏன்?
explanation: This couplet questions the inconsistency in human behavior regarding fate. When destiny brings good things, people readily accept them as natural and positive. Therefore, the poet asks why the same people feel sorrowful and distressed when destiny inevitably brings misfortune. The word அன்று usually means 'not that', but here it is used as the direct opposite of நன்று (good) to mean bad or evil fortune. Recognizing that both good and bad are part of the same natural order helps one maintain equanimity.
